prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Meet Your Desktop Companion", "Your pet lives on your desktop screen! Click and drag them around anytime.", "Got It"]
1: ["Save Your New Pet", "Sign in to sync your companion across desktop sessions."]
2: ["Select Your Desktop Pet", "Choose your primary desktop companion from the available pet list."]
3: ["Listen to Your Pet", "Test pet sound effects and voice interactions before completing adoption.", "Continue"]
4: ["Your Pet Lives in Your System Tray", "Look for the pet icon in your taskbar or menu bar to hide, show, or interact with your companion anytime."]
5: ["Your pet configuration automatically saves to this account so you never lose progress."]
6: ["Configuring desktop overlay graphics...", "Initializing pet behavior engine...", "Preparing tray icon control..."]
7: ["We'll send a system alert as soon as your pet is ready on your desktop."]
8: ["Desktop Shortcut Enabled", "Launch your pet anytime directly from your desktop."]
9: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Pet", "Choose how you would like to create your companion."]
